name: Kani (Gonin-Kan)
description: Kani (also known as Gonin-Kan or Etori) is a sophisticated partnership trick-taking game popular in Aomori Prefecture, Japan. Played by 5 or 6 players, it uses a 50-card deck and features a hidden partnership system where the holder of the Joker and the Ace of trumps work together (the 'Kankei') against the other three players (the 'Mukankei'). It is known for its intense card-counting and localized tournament culture.
deck: 50 cards (Standard 52 minus 2 of H, D, C, plus one Joker)

overview.description: Kani (also known as Gonin-Kan or Etori) is a sophisticated partnership trick-taking game popular in Aomori Prefecture, Japan. Played by 5 or 6 players, it uses a 50-card deck and features a hidden partnership system where the holder of the Joker and the Ace of trumps work together (the 'Kankei') against the other three players (the 'Mukankei'). It is known for its intense card-counting and localized tournament culture.
overview.deck: 50 cards (Standard 52 minus 2 of H, D, C, plus one Joker)

history.origins: Originates from the Goshogawara and Tsugaru regions of Aomori. It belongs to the 'Etori' (picture-taking) family of Japanese trick-taking games, which were influenced by 18th-century Western card games via Nagasaki.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Regional tournaments in Aomori standardize the 'Gonin-Kan' (5-person Kan) rules.
1980s: Recognized as a unique regional cultural activity in Northern Japan.
Present: Actively played in community centers and regional clubs; specialized 'Kan' decks are sometimes used.
history.cultural: In Aomori, Kani is more than a game; it is a social bond, with the 'Kankei' (Related) and 'Mukankei' (Unrelated) roles mirroring community hierarchies.
history.evolution: The game evolved from simpler 'Etori' variants into a highly competitive partnership game where the Joker serves as a master trump but with restricted play across tricks.

setup.players: 5 active players. (In 6-player games, the dealer sits out).
setup.deck: 50 cards (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, but remove 2H, 2D, 2C) + 1 Joker.
setup.dealing: Counter-clockwise. Each player receives 10 cards. Trumps (Yaku) rotate: Clubs -> Diamonds -> Hearts -> Spades.
setup.equipment: Standard cards, score sheet, chips for scoring.

rules.objective: Capture 'Point Cards' (A, K, Q, J of each suit). There are 16 points total in the deck.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Partnership**: The player with the **Joker** and the player with the **Ace of Trumps** form the 'Kankei' team. The other three players are the 'Mukankei' team. 2. **The Joker**: The Joker is the strongest card but cannot be played to the first or last trick of a round. 3. **Play**: Counter-clockwise. Must follow suit. If unable, play any card. Highest trump wins; if no trump, highest card of led suit wins.
keyRules: Secret partnership: Joker holder + Ace of trumps = Kankei team
Joker restrictions: Cannot be played in first or last trick
Joker strength: Beats all cards including trumps when played
Card values: A-K-Q-J = 1 point each (16 total points in deck)
Follow suit: Must follow led suit if possible; can play any card if void
Exchange: The Joker/Ace pair can trade one card to optimize their hands before play begins
Kankei wins with 9+ points; capturing all 16 is 'Gyaku Juuroku' (Reverse 16) worth triple

strategy.basic: If you are in the Mukankei (the team of three), you must coordinate to drain the Kankei's Joker and Ace of Trumps as early as possible. If you hold a King and your partner holds the Queen, force the Ace out.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Tome-Suppe' (Spade Stop): In the final round of a match (Spades as trump), save your high spades to prevent the Kankei from achieving a 16-point sweep.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting: Since there are only 50 cards and 16 points, expert players know exactly which face cards remain after the 6th trick. Use this to determine if you can afford to lose a trick to save a high card.
tips: The Joker cannot be used in the first trickâ€”use this opportunity to lead a suit where you think the Ace partner might be weak.
Always track the dealer (Maki-yaku); their team stays in power for 3 rounds if they win.

scoring.description: Points are awarded based on scoring cards captured in tricks. Only Aces, Kings, Queens, and Jacks count (1 point each, 16 total).
scoring.winCondition: The Kankei team needs 9+ points to win the deal. Game typically played to a target match score.

synthesis.shortDescription: A sophisticated Japanese trick-taking game from Aomori with hidden partnerships and rotating trumps. The Joker holder and Ace of trumps form a secret team against three opponents.
